messages.content:
You are writing for a bank's internal auditor, in UK English.
For each finding, write 2-3 plain sentences: what is wrong, why it matters, what to do.
Use ONLY the numbers given. Do not add, round, combine or calculate numbers.
Do not name customers. Return JSON: {"findings": {"<id>": "<text>", ...}}

{"CV1": "Money order deposits (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions. No rule can fire on money order deposits (in), so £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for money order deposits (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "BL1": "50 customers with no case look highly unusual. top 50 of 47,056 unflagged customers. These customers never reached the alarm level, but their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Top reasons: 6334452196: money in (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 22 (top 0.5% of customers) | 1896192273: money in from abroad (£) 333,931 (top 0.7% of customers); most payments in 30 days 247 (top 1% of customers); money in (£) 333,931 (top 1% of customers) | 8961996693: money in (£) 447,072 (top 0.3% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 406,901 (top 0.4% of customers); most deposits in one day 2 (top 2% of customers) Suggested fix: Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.", "BL3": "The valued-client list hides highly unusual customers. 5 of 5 suppressed customers in the top 2% most unusual. These customers scored enough for a case but were exempted as valued clients, and their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Suggested fix: Remove automatic suppression; review valued clients like anyone else.", "AD1": "Advisory pattern not caught: Business credit‑card repayments to many individuals. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £2,115,842. The advisory warns: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\". 25 customers match this pattern, but only a transaction-count rule can see them, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: Assume at least ten distinct cardholders over a 90‑day window; each repayment between £250‑£2,500 Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: business credit‑card repayments to many individuals (red flag: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\").", "AD2": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple small money orders paid in same day. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £668,454. The advisory warns: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\". 25 customers match this pattern, but no rule can see these transactions, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: Assume at least two money orders per day, combined total <£2,500, repeated on at least two separate days Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple small money orders paid in same day (red flag: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\").", "CV2": "Credit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,095,313,643. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card payments (out).", "CV3": "Debit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,085,585,977. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for debit card payments (out).", "CV4": "Credit card repayments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £63,913,161. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card repayments (out).", "CA1": "Weak rule over-weighted: R01_large_cash. 10 pts, right 1.5% of the time (1-3%, n=529). Cash deposit at or over £10,000. Only 2% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 10 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 points to cut false alarms.", "CA2": "Weak rule over-weighted: R04_large_wire. 5 pts, right 4.1% of the time (3-6%, n=999). Wire or cross-border payment of £50,000 or more. Only 4% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 5 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 points to cut false alarms."}

reply: {"findings":{"CV1":"Money order deposits (in) are not monitored at all – 0% of £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions were checked. This means £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers was never screened, creating a blind spot for potential illicit activity. Add monitoring scenarios for money order deposits, including amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","BL1":"Fifty customers with no case are among the most unusual of the 47,056 unflagged customers. Their activity includes money in of £831,312 (top 0.1% of customers) and £333,931 (top 0.7% of customers), money in from abroad of £831,312 and £333,931, high‑risk‑country transactions of 22, most payments in 30 days of 247 and most deposits in one day of 2. Send these customers for manual review, starting with the highest‑ranked case.","BL3":"The valued‑client list hides five highly unusual customers, all of whom are in the top 2% most unusual. Because they are automatically exempted, their risky behaviour is not examined despite scoring enough for a case. Remove the automatic suppression and review valued clients like any other customer.","AD1":"The advisory for business credit‑card repayments to many individuals matches 25 customers, yet only one case was generated, representing 4% of the matches and £2,115,842 of exposure. The pattern expects repayments to at least ten distinct cardholders over a 90‑day window, each between £250 and £2,500. Add a scenario that flags business credit‑card repayments to many individuals as a red flag.","AD2":"The advisory for multiple small money orders on the same day matches 25 customers, but only one case was generated, representing 4% of the matches and £668,454 of exposure. The rule looks for at least two money orders per day with a combined total just below £2,500, repeated on at least two separate days. Add a scenario to capture this pattern as a red flag.","CV2":"Credit card payments (out) are only screened by a transaction‑count rule, R06_velocity, covering £3,095,313,643. Because amount, country and counter‑party data are ignored, illicit payments could slip through unnoticed. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for credit card payments (out).","CV3":"Debit card payments (out) are only screened by a transaction‑count rule, R06_velocity, covering £3,085,585,977. Because amount, country and counter‑party data are ignored, illicit payments could slip through unnoticed. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for debit card payments (out).","CV4":"Credit card repayments (out) are only screened by a transaction‑count rule, R06_velocity, covering £63,913,161. Because amount, country and counter‑party data are ignored, illicit repayments could slip through unnoticed. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for credit card repayments (out).","CA1":"Rule R01_large_cash carries a weight of 10 points but is correct only 1.5% of the time (range 1‑3%, n=529). With only 2% of reviewed customers flagged by this rule actually laundering, it generates many false alarms. Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 points to cut false alarms.","CA2":"Rule R04_large_wire carries a weight of 5 points but is correct only 4.1% of the time (range 3‑6%, n=999). With only 4% of reviewed customers flagged by this rule actually laundering, it generates many false alarms. Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 points to cut false alarms."}}
